speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether current efforts to educate youths on the harm of drugs have considered (i) the opportunities and challenges arising from the increased availability of mobile devices (ii) the evolving media environment overseas and (iii) the risks of very young Singaporeans inadvertently coming across drug content; and (b) what is being done to keep up the educational efforts with the ongoing and emerging trends of content promoting drugs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They also make it easier for people to procure drugs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: CNB also works with youth advocates, such as students from Institutes of Higher Learning, to ensure that its anti-drug messages and campaigns are relatable to youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: CNB works with MOE and schools to incorporate anti-drug messages into the school curriculum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It engages students through talks, sharing sessions, exhibitions and skits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are also efforts to get parents on board.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: CNB produced a range of anti-drug materials suitable for families with young children for display at these libraries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some of the libraries organised family-friendly activities, such as storytelling and craft sessions, to raise awareness of the harms of drugs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: CNB also commissioned editorials in The Straits Times' "Smart Parenting" column to highlight the important role of parental guidance in drug issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have met Clementi parents who are worried about foreign drug cartels and foreign influence and sponsorship that may be leading to a proliferation of drug lifestyle, media and related contents that may find its way into the handphones and mobile devices that their children are using.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, can I ask the Minister of State two supplementary questions?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That is something, from the operational perspective, that we do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is where we target persons who share harmful information regarding drugs, particularly online to influence others towards the commission of drug activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to navigate this because we also look at issues, not only in the upstream, but we are also looking at the operational and intelligence angle, and we continue to improve and be ahead of what the cartels or syndicates are doing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Member asked a question about the most commonly abused drugs among youths.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we also want the youths to feel empowered.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have been working with them to co-create not only to produce the information materials but co-create the feeling of being empowered to stay drug-free.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Recently, we had youths from Hong Kong visiting us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we also involve our youths in this process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As a whole, it is not only about Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to make sure that our youths also understand why drugs are so harmful, not only within the Singapore context but also beyond and how they can play a part in this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We need to work with youths and the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, while we continue to engage via online means, we also do not forget the face-to-face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That is where we engage parents – we share with them what they should do, some of the signs and symptoms of when their child is taking drugs and so forth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is hard work but meaningful and worthwhile, to keep Singapore safe and secure.
